e-620.knowledge_point: Finding the Acceleration Vector of a Particle Given Its Velocity Vector
e-620.problem:
The velocity vector $\mathbf{v} = \langle u, v \rangle$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
\mathbf{v} = \langle 12t+t^2, t^3+1\rangle.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $\mathbf{a}$.
e-620.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(12t+{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}+1)⟩ \\  & =⟨12+2t,\,3{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

e-7224.knowledge_point: Computing the Acceleration of a Particle at a Given Moment Given Its Velocity Vector
e-7224.problem:
The velocity vector $\mathbf{v} = \langle u, v \rangle,$ measured in $\textrm{m}/\textrm s,$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ seconds, is given by

$$
\mathbf{v} = \langle t^4-t^2, 2t^3\rangle.
$$

Find the acceleration vector and the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1.$
e-7224.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4}-{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨4{t}^{3}-2t,\,6{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(1) & =⟨4(1)^{3}-2(1),6(1)^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨2,6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|\mathbf a(1)|\mathbin{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(1)| & =|⟨2,6⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{6}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{40} \\  & =2\sqrt{10}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

e-621.knowledge_point: Finding the Acceleration Vector of a Particle Given Its Position Vector
e-621.problem:
The position vector $\mathbf{r}$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
\mathbf{r} = \langle 4t^2+1, 3t^2-t\rangle.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $\mathbf{a}$.
e-621.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector. We can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{2}+1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}-t)⟩ \\  & =⟨8t,\,6t-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6t-1)⟩ \\  & =⟨8,6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

e-7225.knowledge_point: Computing the Acceleration of a Particle at a Given Moment Given Its Position Vector
e-7225.problem:
The position vector $\mathbf{r},$ in meters, of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$
\mathbf{r} = \left\langle t^{5}-t^2,\, t^2+6t-3 \right\rangle.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector and the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=0.$
e-7225.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{5}-{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+6t-3)⟩ \\  & =⟨5{t}^{4}-2t,\,2t+6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5{t}^{4}-2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t+6)⟩ \\  & =⟨20{t}^{3}-2,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=0,$ we substitute $t=0$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(0) & =⟨20(0)^{3}-2,\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|\mathbf a(0)|\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(0)| & =|⟨-2,\,2⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{8} \\  & =2\sqrt{2}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

after.html:
Question 2
?

The velocity vector v=⟨u,v⟩ of a particle P at time t is given by v=⟨5t−8,2t2+4⟩. Calculate the acceleration vector a.

a
a=⟨−8,4⟩
b
a=⟨5,2⟩
c
a=⟨5,2t⟩
d
a=⟨5,4t⟩
e
a=⟨5t,2t2⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

a=dvdt=⟨dudt,dvdt⟩=⟨ddt(5t−8),ddt(2t2+4)⟩=⟨5,4t⟩

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms that acceleration is the derivative of velocity: d(5t-8)/dt=5 and d(2t^2+4)/dt=4t. Therefore option d is correct; the deliberately submitted option a is incorrect.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Acceleration Vector of a Particle Given Its Velocity Vector
content.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
v=⟨5t-8,\,2{t}^{2}+4⟩.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a.$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5t-8),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2}+4)⟩ \\  & =⟨5,\,4t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 5
?

The velocity vector v=⟨u,v⟩ of a particle P at time t is given by v=⟨4t2,−332t4⟩. Calculate the acceleration vector a.

a
a(t)=⟨8t,−316t3⟩
b
a(t)=⟨8,−98t2⟩
c
a(t)=⟨8t,−38t3⟩
d
a(t)=⟨8t,−3160t5⟩
e
a(t)=⟨43t3,−3160t5⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: Differentiate each velocity component: d(4t^2)/dt=8t and d(-(3/32)t^4)/dt=-(12/32)t^3=-(3/8)t^3. Thus option c is correct.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
v=⟨4{t}^{2},\,-\frac{3}{32}{t}^{4}⟩.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{3}{32}{t}^{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨8t,\,-\frac{3}{8}{t}^{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Acceleration Vector of a Particle Given Its Velocity Vector
content.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
v=⟨4{t}^{2},\,-\frac{3}{32}{t}^{4}⟩.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a.$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{3}{32}{t}^{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨8t,\,-\frac{3}{8}{t}^{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 7
?

The velocity vector v=⟨u,v⟩, measured in m/s, of a particle P at time t seconds is given by v=⟨2t−1,1t2+1⟩. Find the magnitude of the acceleration of P at time t=1.

a
4ln2⁡2+12m/s2
b
2ln2⁡2+14m/s2
c
2ln⁡2+12m/s2
d
4ln⁡2+14m/s2
e
ln2⁡2+12m/s2
Submit

decision.explanation: Differentiating gives a(t)=⟨2^{t-1}ln(2),-2t/(t^2+1)^2⟩. At t=1 this is ⟨ln(2),-1/2⟩, whose magnitude is sqrt((ln(2))^2+1/4)=sqrt(4(ln(2))^2+1)/2 m/s². This matches option a.

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩,$ measured in $\text{m}/\text{s},$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$
v=⟨{2}^{t-1},\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}⟩.
$$

Find the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({2}^{t-1}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1})⟩ \\  & =⟨{2}^{t-1}\operatorname{ln}⁡2,-\frac{2t}{({t}^{2}+1)^{2}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(1) & =⟨{2}^{1-1}\operatorname{ln}⁡2,-\frac{2(1)}{({1}^{2}+1)^{2}}⟩ \\  & =⟨{2}^{0}\operatorname{ln}⁡2,-\frac{2}{4}⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡2,-\frac{1}{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|a(1)|:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(1)| & =|⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡2,-\frac{1}{2}⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)^{2}+{(-\frac{1}{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{ln}^{2}⁡2+\frac{1}{4}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{4{ln}^{2}⁡2+1}{4}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{4{ln}^{2}⁡2+1}}{2}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7
?

The velocity vector v=⟨u,v⟩, measured in m/s, of a particle P at time t seconds is given by v=⟨2t−1,1t2+1⟩. Find the magnitude of the acceleration of P at time t=1.

a
4ln2⁡2+12m/s2
b
2ln2⁡2+14m/s2
c
2ln⁡2+12m/s2
d
4ln⁡2+14m/s2
e
ln2⁡2+12m/s2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector: a=dvdt=⟨dudt,dvdt⟩=⟨ddt(2t−1),ddt(1t2+1)⟩=⟨2t−1ln⁡2,−2t(t2+1)2⟩

To find the acceleration at time t=1, we substitute t=1 into the above: a(1)=⟨21−1ln⁡2,−2(1)(12+1)2⟩=⟨20ln⁡2,−24⟩=⟨ln⁡2,−12⟩

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute |a(1)|: |a(1)|=|⟨ln⁡2,−12⟩|=(ln⁡2)2+(−12)2=ln2⁡2+14=4ln2⁡2+14=4ln2⁡2+12m/s2.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms a(1)=⟨ln(2),-1/2⟩. Its magnitude is sqrt((ln(2))^2+1/4)=sqrt(4(ln(2))^2+1)/2 m/s², matching option a. The deliberately submitted option e is incorrect.

content.knowledge_point: Computing the Acceleration of a Particle at a Given Moment Given Its Velocity Vector
content.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩,$ measured in $\text{m}/\text{s},$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$
v=⟨{2}^{t-1},\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}⟩.
$$

Find the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1.$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({2}^{t-1}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1})⟩ \\  & =⟨{2}^{t-1}\operatorname{ln}⁡2,-\frac{2t}{({t}^{2}+1)^{2}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(1) & =⟨{2}^{1-1}\operatorname{ln}⁡2,-\frac{2(1)}{({1}^{2}+1)^{2}}⟩ \\  & =⟨{2}^{0}\operatorname{ln}⁡2,-\frac{2}{4}⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡2,-\frac{1}{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|a(1)|:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(1)| & =|⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡2,-\frac{1}{2}⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)^{2}+{(-\frac{1}{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{ln}^{2}⁡2+\frac{1}{4}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{4{ln}^{2}⁡2+1}{4}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{4{ln}^{2}⁡2+1}}{2}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
v=⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡(3t+1),1-{t}^{2}⟩,\,t>0.

Calculate the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t=2.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3t+1)),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3}{3t+1},-2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the acceleration at time $t=2,$ we substitute $t=2$ into the above:

$$

Question 8
?

The velocity vector v=⟨u,v⟩ of a particle P at time t is given by v=⟨ln⁡(3t+1),1−t2⟩,t>0. Calculate the acceleration vector a at time t=2.

a
a(2)=⟨37,−2⟩
b
a(2)=⟨35,−7⟩
c
a(2)=⟨ln⁡7,−4⟩
d
a(2)=⟨37,−4⟩
e
a(2)=⟨ln⁡3,−7⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector: a=dvdt=⟨dudt,dvdt⟩=⟨ddt(ln⁡(3t+1)),ddt(1−t2)⟩=⟨33t+1,−2t⟩

Finally, to find the acceleration at time t=2, we substitute t=2 into the above: a(2)=⟨33(2)+1,−2(2)⟩=⟨37,−4⟩

content.knowledge_point: Computing the Acceleration of a Particle at a Given Moment Given Its Velocity Vector
content.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
v=⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡(3t+1),1-{t}^{2}⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t=2.$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3t+1)),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3}{3t+1},-2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the acceleration at time $t=2,$ we substitute $t=2$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(2) & =⟨\frac{3}{3(2)+1},-2(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3}{7},-4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

The velocity vector v=⟨u,v⟩, measured in m/s, of a particle P at time t seconds is given by v=⟨−22cos⁡2t,2sin⁡2t⟩. Find the magnitude of the acceleration of P at time t=π8.

a
5m/s2
b
5m/s2
c
52m/s2
d
2m/s2
e
25m/s2

decision.explanation: Differentiating gives a(t)=⟨4√2 sin(2t),2√2 cos(2t)⟩. At t=π/8, sin(π/4)=cos(π/4)=√2/2, so a=⟨4,2⟩. Its magnitude is √(16+4)=2√5 m/s², option e.

The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩,$ measured in $\text{m}/\text{s},$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$
v=⟨-2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t⟩.
$$

Find the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=\frac{\pi }{8}.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨4\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=\frac{\pi }{8},$ we substitute $t=\frac{\pi }{8}$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(\frac{\pi }{8}) & =⟨4\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{8}),2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{8})⟩ \\  & =⟨4\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}),2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨4\sqrt{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},2\sqrt{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨4,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|a(\frac{\pi }{8})|:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(\frac{\pi }{8})| & =|⟨4,2⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16+4} \\  & =\sqrt{20} \\  & =2\sqrt{5}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The velocity vector v=⟨u,v⟩, measured in m/s, of a particle P at time t seconds is given by v=⟨−22cos⁡2t,2sin⁡2t⟩. Find the magnitude of the acceleration of P at time t=π8.

a
5m/s2
b
5m/s2
c
52m/s2
d
2m/s2
e
25m/s2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector: a=dvdt=⟨dudt,dvdt⟩=⟨ddt(−22cos⁡2t),ddt(2sin⁡2t)⟩=⟨42sin⁡2t,22cos⁡2t⟩

To find the acceleration at time t=π8, we substitute t=π8 into the above: a(π8)=⟨42sin⁡(2⋅π8),22cos⁡(2⋅π8)⟩=⟨42sin⁡(π4),22cos⁡(π4)⟩=⟨42⋅22,22⋅22⟩=⟨4,2⟩

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute |a(π8)|: |a(π8)|=|⟨4,2⟩|=42+22=16+4=20=25m/s2

$$

$$

Find the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=\frac{\pi }{8}.$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨4\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=\frac{\pi }{8},$ we substitute $t=\frac{\pi }{8}$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(\frac{\pi }{8}) & =⟨4\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{8}),2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{8})⟩ \\  & =⟨4\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}),2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨4\sqrt{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},2\sqrt{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨4,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|a(\frac{\pi }{8})|:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(\frac{\pi }{8})| & =|⟨4,2⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16+4} \\  & =\sqrt{20} \\  & =2\sqrt{5}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩,$ measured in $\text{m}/\text{s},$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$
v=⟨3{t}^{2}+2t-1,-4t+5⟩.
$$

Find the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1\,\text{s}.$ Do not round the answer.

The magnitude of the acceleration is
{{field-1}}
${\text{m/s}}^{2}.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}+2t-1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-4t+5)⟩ \\  & =⟨6t+2,\,-4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(1) & =⟨6(1)+2,-4⟩ \\  & =⟨8,-4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|a(1)|:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(1)| & =|⟨8,-4⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{{8}^{2}+(-4)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{64+16} \\  & =\sqrt{80} \\  & =4\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the magnitude of the acceleration at time $t=1\,\text{s}$ is $4\sqrt{5}{\text{ m/s}}^{2}.$

$$
r(t)=⟨{t}^{3}-4{t}^{2},\,2{t}^{4}-{t}^{2}⟩.

$a=⟨${{field-1}},{{field-2}}$⟩$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-4{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{4}-{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨3{t}^{2}-8t,\,8{t}^{3}-2t⟩\end{aligned}

content.problem:
The position vector $r(t)$ of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
r(t)=⟨{t}^{3}-4{t}^{2},\,2{t}^{4}-{t}^{2}⟩.
$$

Calculate the components of the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t.$

$a=⟨${{field-1}},{{field-2}}$⟩$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-4{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{4}-{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨3{t}^{2}-8t,\,8{t}^{3}-2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}-8t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8{t}^{3}-2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨6t-8,\,24{t}^{2}-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

after.html:
Question 12
?

The position vector r of a particle P (relative to a fixed origin O) at time t is given by r=⟨t55,3t2−1⟩. Calculate the acceleration vector a.

a
a=⟨4t3,6t⟩
b
a=⟨4t3,6⟩
c
a=⟨t3,3⟩
d
a=⟨t4,3t⟩
e
a=⟨6t3,4⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

v=drdt=⟨dxdt,dydt⟩=⟨ddt(t55),ddt(3t2−1)⟩=⟨t4,6t⟩

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

a=dvdt=⟨dudt,dvdt⟩=⟨ddt(t4),ddt(6t)⟩=⟨4t3,6⟩

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms that differentiating position gives velocity ⟨t^4,6t⟩, and differentiating again gives acceleration ⟨4t^3,6⟩. Thus option b is correct.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Acceleration Vector of a Particle Given Its Position Vector
content.problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨\frac{{t}^{5}}{5},\,3{t}^{2}-1⟩.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a.$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{t}^{5}}{5}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}-1)⟩ \\  & =⟨{t}^{4},\,6t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6t)⟩ \\  & =⟨4{t}^{3},\,6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 14
?

The position vector r(t) of a particle P relative to a fixed origin O at time t is given by r(t)=⟨t2−1,e2t+5⟩. Calculate the acceleration vector a.

a
a=⟨2t,4e2t+5⟩
b
a=⟨2t,2e2t+5⟩
c
a=⟨2,e2t+5⟩
d
a=⟨2,2e2t+5⟩
e
a=⟨2,4e2t+5⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: Acceleration is the second derivative of position. Differentiating once gives ⟨2t,2e^{2t+5}⟩, and differentiating again gives ⟨2,4e^{2t+5}⟩. Thus option e is correct.

after.name: Question 14
after.problem:
The position vector $r(t)$ of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
r(t)=⟨{t}^{2}-1,{e}^{2t+5}⟩.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-1),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{2t+5})⟩ \\  & =⟨2t,2{e}^{2t+5}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{e}^{2t+5})⟩ \\  & =⟨2,4{e}^{2t+5}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 14
?

The position vector r(t) of a particle P relative to a fixed origin O at time t is given by r(t)=⟨t2−1,e2t+5⟩. Calculate the acceleration vector a.

a
a=⟨2t,4e2t+5⟩
b
a=⟨2t,2e2t+5⟩
c
a=⟨2,e2t+5⟩
d
a=⟨2,2e2t+5⟩
e
a=⟨2,4e2t+5⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector: v=drdt=⟨dxdt,dydt⟩=⟨ddt(t2−1),ddt(e2t+5)⟩=⟨2t,2e2t+5⟩

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector: a=dvdt=⟨dudt,dvdt⟩=⟨ddt(2t),ddt(2e2t+5)⟩=⟨2,4e2t+5⟩

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms that acceleration is the second derivative of position: ⟨2,4e^{2t+5}⟩. Each differentiation of the exponential contributes a factor of 2, so option e is correct.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Acceleration Vector of a Particle Given Its Position Vector
content.problem:
The position vector $r(t)$ of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
r(t)=⟨{t}^{2}-1,{e}^{2t+5}⟩.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a.$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-1),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{2t+5})⟩ \\  & =⟨2t,2{e}^{2t+5}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{e}^{2t+5})⟩ \\  & =⟨2,4{e}^{2t+5}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

r=⟨{t}^{3}-4{t}^{2}+2,\,5+{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}⟩.
$$

Calculate the components of the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t=1.$ Do not round the answers.

$a(1)=⟨${{field-1}},{{field-2}}$⟩$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do by differentiating the position vector:

Question 19
?

The position vector r of a particle P (relative to a fixed origin O) at time t is given by r=⟨4−2t2,1−3t3⟩. Calculate the acceleration vector a at time t=1.

a
a(1)=⟨−2,−18⟩
b
a(1)=⟨−4,−18⟩
c
a(1)=⟨−8,−12⟩
d
a(1)=⟨−2,−12⟩
e
a(1)=⟨−4,−9⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: Differentiate position twice: velocity is ⟨-4t,-9t²⟩ and acceleration is ⟨-4,-18t⟩. At t=1, acceleration is ⟨-4,-18⟩, option b.

after.name: Question 19
after.problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨4-2{t}^{2},1-3{t}^{3}⟩.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t=1.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4-2{t}^{2}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-3{t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨-4t,-9{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-4t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-9{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,-18t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the acceleration at time $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(1) & =⟨-4,-18(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,-18⟩\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨4-2{t}^{2},1-3{t}^{3}⟩.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t=1.$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4-2{t}^{2}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-3{t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨-4t,-9{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-4t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-9{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,-18t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the acceleration at time $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(1) & =⟨-4,-18(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,-18⟩\end{aligned}
$$
